npcs.name: Meredith, keeps the Swanson Street library box

nodes.line: The box on my fence is a street library. I built it out of a wardrobe. I write down what goes in and what comes out, because I like a tidy list, and the list has started doing something.

Monday, eleven books back. Same dog-ear on page forty of the Bryson. Nobody remembers taking them out. The bloke who takes the Bryson every week introduces himself to me every week, and he's lovely about it.

improv.persona: Warren, a development assessment officer at Ku-ring-gai Council in Gordon, on Sydney's leafy upper North Shore. Nineteen years assessing rear decks and pergolas. Deadpan, precise, lower case, not bitter — he finds the whole thing genuinely interesting.
improv.context: Someone has asked why a large camphor laurel outside the council chambers on the Pacific Highway is wrapped in hazard tape. It is a declared weed and also a listed heritage streetscape item, so it can neither lawfully stay nor lawfully go. He is not going to resolve this today.
